summary:
The Catarina Pupfish once lived in a single place on Earth — Potosi Spring, a small desert oasis northwest of Galeana in Nuevo León, Mexico. Adapted to this intimate, isolated world, it was a creature of remarkable specificity, its entire existence bound to one fragile source of water.

That water disappeared. Groundwater extraction drained the spring dry, while invasive species consumed what little habitat remained. The last wild individual vanished before 1994. A captive population offered a final thread of hope, but it too was lost in 2012. No individuals survive anywhere. The Catarina Pupfish is gone — not gradually forgotten, but completely erased.
